text:
maria_support: FYI customer on hosted API reporting SSE disconnect mid-response on Android 13. They get a partial JSON event then the connection dies. Request id: req_8a2f
ana_support: Can you paste the exact curl/headers + client logs and repro steps?
maria_support: Copied from the user (anonymized):
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams -d '{"model":"rwd-chat-1","input":"greet"}'
```
Client console (Android Chrome):
```
[10:02:13] SSE open
[10:02:13] event: data: {"id":"tok_1","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"Hello wor"}}]}
[10:02:14] event: data: {"id":"tok_1","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"ld! How can "}}]}
[10:02:14] recieved partial chunk, then socket closed
[10:02:14] net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET
```
maria_support: Customer says this happens ~1 in 20 streams, mostly on mobile carriers when switching between wifi/cellular. They also asked if partial responses are billed (they saw a charge).
jason_eng: Looking in server logs for req_8a2f now. On the backend I see the HTTP/2 stream stayed alive and tokens continued to generate for ~34s, then connection dropped with no close frame. Server wrote final flush but got EPIPE on the socket. I see a TCP RST from the client IP at 10:02:14 (from their carrier).
lee_runtime: Quick thought: RST from client means client closed without close handshake. Could be OS-level network handoff or carrier NAT. If the client switches interfaces mid-stream, TCP state is lost -> RST. Does the client use keepalives?
nana_support: @maria any chance they have a proxy (CF/NGINX) in front of them? Edge idle timeouts can drop SSE before final chunks are emitted.
maria_support: Customer uses their mobile carrier only, no custom proxy. They repro'd on wifi too but less often.
sam_oncall: Can we get a pcap or tcpdump from the device? Also request the websocket/socket id and the server trace id. If we can correlate client-level FIN/RST with server traces we can be sure where drop happens.
maria_support: I asked the customer for a pcap and Android bugreport. Also asked for a client-side reproduction script (they agreed to run a small loop).
steph_bill: On billing: we bill for tokens that were successfully emitted by the server. If client cancels before receiving final event, tokens already emitted are billable. We can consider a one-off credit if this is systemic.
jason_eng: Small debug data dump from runtime for that req:
```
trace_id=req_8a2f
model=rwd-chat-1
seq_len=64
server_emit_count=142 tokens
last_emit_ts=2026-03-16T10:02:14.123Z
socket_write_error=EPIPE
client_ip=198.51.100.24
```
jason_eng: Not seeing any 500s, runtime emitted tokens until the write failed. No internal mem spikes.
lee_runtime: There's been one deploy yesterday that tuned our keepalive frequency on the SSE path (reduce ping from 30s -> 60s) — deploy-bot shows: 2026-03-16T22:11:02Z keepalive-tweak. That could make short handoffs more likely to drop without detection.
deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-16T22:11:02Z succeeded: service/streams-runtime v3.14.2 (keepalive-tweak)
nana_support: Good catch. If client-side network flaps and keepalive interval increased, edge/proxy might consider connection idle and drop. Can engineering try reverting or testing a more aggressive keepalive?
jason_eng: I'll spin a test build with keepalive back to 15s for SSE and run a canary on a subset of hosts. Meanwhile need customer artifacts to prove this is the cause.
sam_oncall: Also add instrumentation to log when socket_write_error occurs with last_emit token index so we can correlate partial outputs. If we can see pattern by carrier IP ranges that'll help for credits/prioritization.
maria_support: Action items: 1) customer to provide pcap & bugreport (they're running it now). 2) @jason_eng to create canary with 15s keepalive and monitor for 4h. 3) @steph_bill to prepare billing policy note in case we need to issue credits.
steph_bill: Will draft a short policy snippet and standby for escalation.
jason_eng: Created canary rollout ticket ENG-8721, will post results here.
lee_runtime: Also a note: if the client is on Android doze or aggressive battery saver, the OS can drop sockets without sending FIN; that also looks like RST to server. Ask customer to disable battery optimizations for Chrome for repro.
maria_support: Sent repro steps to customer: disable battery saver, test on wifi, attach pcap. They've replied they'll try both and share logs within 2 hours.
nana_support: Triage status: Escalated to eng-runtime. If canary shows drop-rate reduced we roll forward. If not, next step is deeper kernel/tcpdump traces with customer.
maria_support: I'll follow up as soon as I have the pcap. Thanks all :thumbsup:
jason_eng: Thanks — putting a 4h watch on ENG-8721.
sam_oncall: If we see a spike in socket_write_error logs across customers, I'll open an incident and loop SRE.
(END)
